bullets.text: UBS cuts Amber FY27-29E earnings 26-33% on margin headwinds, higher minority interest and depreciation; Q2 PAT may stay negative despite 59% EBITDA growth.

detail.summary: UBS sees Amber's Q2 top line driven largely by acquisitions, so reported growth overstates organic momentum. Below EBITDA, depreciation and minority interest absorb the gain, leaving PAT negative. The cut sits inside a sector-wide margin-led de-rating.

Q2 revenue +28% YoY, led by electronics
Q2 EBITDA +59%, largely acquisition-driven
PAT may be negative on depreciation and minority interest

bullets.text: Counterpoint sees festive-season India smartphone volumes -12% YoY on memory-cost-led price rises, with value +5% on higher ASPs.
bullets.source: Nomura (Bera) — India Consumer Durables and EMS: As smartphone prices rise, consumers wait for festive sales to buy (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Higher memory costs and device prices are cutting festive volumes while consumers trade up selectively via financing and trade-ins. Component costs are still rising, so prices could climb further. Channel conversion depends on financing, trade-in and promotional offers, a volume headwind for smartphone EMS.
points: Festive smartphone volume -12% YoY
Market value +5% YoY on higher ASPs

bullets.text: El Nino drag lands in 2HFY27: CLSA says kharif output falls 7-10% on 6-8% yield loss even with area sown down only 1%.
bullets.source: CLSA — India economics: Wait for El Nino impact in 2HFY27 (+7 more in Outlook, unread)

detail.summary: The rainfall deficit was c.13% while area sown fell just 1%, which markets read as no monsoon damage. CLSA argues area sown is the wrong gauge: past El Nino years show the hit comes through yields, rural wages and agri GVA, concentrated in the second half.
points: Rainfall deficit c.13%; area sown down only 1%
Historical yield fall of 6-8% in El Nino years
Kharif production down 7-10% historically
